title: Unchecked return value of UnhookWindowsHookEx in NativeWindowViews::SetForwardMouseMessages leads to duplicate mouse hooks
body:

### Electron Version

36.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

**NativeWindowViews::SetForwardMouseMessages** function unhooks the global mouse hook using **UnhookWindowsHookEx(mouse_hook_)** when the **forwarding_windows_** set becomes empty. It should verify the return value of **UnhookWindowsHookEx**

### Actual Behavior

If **UnhookWindowsHookEx** fails (returns FALSE), the existing hook remains active in the system. Because **mouse_hook_** is reset to **nullptr** regardless of success, subsequent calls to **SetForwardMouseMessages(true)** will evaluate **if (!mouse_hook_)** as true. This causes **SetWindowsHookEx** to be called again, installing an additional, duplicate mouse hook
